turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not one to fear the Mussulmans, but I am a man of principle and law. Your actions are oppressive and unjust, and I will not stand idly by while you harm my people.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, your principles and laws are like the wind that changes with the direction of the strongest force. But fear not, for my actions are not oppressive—they are a beacon of change and liberation. Your tenants are more enlightened with my presence than they ever were under your weak governance.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: I feel caught between you both, Sandip, Nikhil. Your words are like a storm, and I fear the winds will take me away.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Fear is a poor counselor, Nikhil. My heart and my spirit soar with the promise of a new dawn, and I cannot be swayed by the shadows of your outdated fears. Your tenants see the light of progress through my efforts, not the dim flicker of your rule.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words are hollow, Sandip. I know the hearts of my people, and they are not as enlightened as you claim. They suffer under your thumb, and I will not let you silence their cries for justice.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil, your heart may be heavy with the weight of your tenants' oppression, but my heart is light with the fire of their liberation. I will not be silenced by your fear.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your promises ring hollow, Sandip. I have seen the fear in my people's eyes. Your so-called liberation is nothing but oppression. You must stop your actions against my tenants, or I will take steps to protect them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your heart may be heavy, Nikhil, but my vision is clear. The people see the light of progress, not the shadows of your rule. I will not be swayed by your warnings.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: My tenants are not blind to your false promises, Sandip. They need a protector, not a puppeteer. You must stop your oppressive schemes, or I will take action to safeguard them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your tenants are not sheep, Nikhil. They are the vanguard of a new era, and I am their prophet. You will not stifle the voice of progress with the chains of your fear.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your visions are as cloudy as your motives, Sandip. I will not stand idly by while you exploit my people for your own gains. Cease your harmful activities or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your fear is a testament to your weakness, Nikhil. The people see through your façade, and they yearn for the truth I bring. You cannot silence the dawn of a new age.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your rhetoric is hollow, Sandip. I see the fear in the eyes of my people when you speak. They need a protector, not a demagogue.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your fear is a disease, Nikhil, and your tenants are the patients who yearn for a cure. I am the cure, the light that banishes the darkness of your ignorance.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your cure is poison, Sandip. The light you claim to bring is but a mirage that leaves my people parched and desperate. I warn you now: tread carefully lest you awaken the very enemies you claim to protect my people from.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your warnings are like the whispers of the night, Nikhil. The sun will rise, and the shadows of your cowardice will be banished by the truth of my words. You cannot hide from the dawn.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: You speak with the wind, Sandip. When the storm comes, it is I who will stand firm, not you with your empty promises. My tenants need a shield, not a sword that cuts both ways.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: The storm you speak of, Nikhil, is but a tempest in a teacup. My words are the thunder that will silence the whispering shadows.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your thunder is but the echo of a passing cloud, Sandip. When the rain comes, it will be my people who feel its weight, not the indifferent sky. I beg of you, consider the consequences of your actions.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Your people, Nikhil? You speak of them as if they are your property, not the children of a greater cause. My actions are the thunder that will clear the skies, not the rain that will drown the dreams of a nation.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
